notes:
Passed on the fake backend only by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: reviewed_by is null, the R2 hardware backend is refused until a human signs it, and nothing ran on a Spot. The driver binds the Robot class: cached RobotId identity, power/E-Stop/arm state, cached usernames, frame names from the frame-tree snapshot, two hardware-configuration flags, the boolean motors_on write through Robot.power_on/power_off, and the native stop power_off(cut_immediately=True); the physical E-Stop button is the independent stop (docs/python/quickstart.md:379). No catalogue requests: cap.device.configure.v1 binds the boolean write and no extension id is used. NOT COVERED: motion and navigation commands (they need RobotCommandClient and a command builder, not the Robot class), mission pause/stop (MissionClient is a separate entry symbol and is not the native class), time sync and lease state (the native factory starts time sync and keeps a body lease for hardware, but no driver state publishes them), and all camera and point-cloud arrays. The fake returns a three-frame stand-in (body, odom, vision) and one cached username; the real frame tree and username cache are device/account dependent, and every canned value is marked # placeholder. The gate reports one warning, G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE: the only actuating input is boolean motors_on, so SAFE-014 has no numeric bound to probe and the suite awards CL2 while every other CL3 test passed; no numeric bound was invented to silence it. driver.lock install.python >=3.7 is python/bosdyn-client/setup.py:57; the SDK is imported only by native.py and is never installed or imported by the gate. gate.digest is the digest the last check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
